articles.title: Is Kyrie Irving the perfect partner for Cooper Flagg?
articles.summary: Here's what a healthy Irving could unlock for Flagg and the Mavericks this season.
articles.body:
The Dallas Mavericks overhauled their front office, hired a new head coach, and reshaped their roster this offseason. But their most important addition on the court could be Kyrie Irving as he returns from a torn ACL. If Kyrie looks like Kyrie, no one will benefit more than Cooper Flagg, who has apparently grown .

Former head coach Jason Kidd spent the start of last season experimenting with Flagg playing point guard. A lot of the time, Flagg looked like a teenager. But by the end of the season, Flagg looked like an All-NBA player. Over his final 26 games, Flagg averaged 25.2 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 5.3 assists. His surge was highlighted by a 51-point performance that helped him win Rookie of the Year.

By bringing the ball up the floor, using screens and reading defenders over hundreds of repetitions, he's better prepared for his career moving forward. However, Flagg and the Mavericks were better when he played with a pure point guard.

When Flagg shared the floor with Ryan Nembhard or Brandon Williams last season, he was more efficient and the Mavericks played better. This doesn't mean that Flagg can't run an offense. It just means that, at least at this stage of his career, he's better when he has help. That's why Irving's mere presence can provide balance to Flagg's offensive diet.

Flagg's magic is that he can be both an initiator and a play finisher. He can grab a rebound and lead the break, run pick-and-roll or attack from the elbows. But he can also cut, screen, roll, spot up, crash the glass and destroy a rotating defense.

Kyrie has already shown he can thrive alongside jumbo playmakers. He won a championship next to LeBron James and excelled alongside Luka Dončić . And though Flagg is nowhere near as accomplished as LeBron or Luka, he brings a versatile skill set that can complement Kyrie. On some plays, Irving can run the show while Flagg moves around off-ball. On other plays, it'll be Flagg who handles the ball and Kyrie can set an inverted screen for him.

Obviously, there's concern around whether Kyrie can stay healthy. He's 34 years old and just missed a full calendar year. But Cooper is the centerpiece now. And together, they're going to have plenty of help.

At center, Daniel Gafford and Dereck Lively II ( who is still recovering from foot surgery ) provide two vertical threats. There's concern over Lively's durability, but that's why drafting Morez Johnson Jr. made so much sense. Johnson is an elite athlete who can switch across positions as a 6-foot-9, 250-pound defender. The Mavericks also brought in Santi Aldama , who is a floor-spacing forward that can do a lot of the little things. P.J. Washington , Max Christie , and Naji Marshall remain on the roster and offer size and versatility — and, who knows, maybe a change of scenery even helps Zaccharie Risacher find a stable rotation role.

Now it's on new head coach Dusty May to put those pieces together. He led FAU to the Final Four and won a national championship in just his second season at Michigan. May said that Flagg will play "all over the court," which should really come as no surprise given how this roster is constructed. The new Dallas front office, led by Masai Ujiri and Mike Schmitz, is already surrounding Flagg with versatile pieces that could translate to immediate wins.

If Irving can return healthy, then we could see Flagg turn into a star and the Mavericks turn into a playoff team a lot sooner than anyone might expect.

articles.title: Un imparable TJ Shorts da la primera victoria al Valencia Basket
articles.standfirst: El base anota 26 puntos en el sufrido triunfo ante el Besiktas, que falló un triple para ganar sobre la bocina
articles.summary: El base anota 26 puntos en el sufrido triunfo ante el Besiktas, que falló un triple para ganar sobre la bocina
articles.body: TJ Shorts deslumbró hace dos temporadas jugando al ritmo frenético del París Basketball. La pasada, sufrió bajo la estructura de Ergin Ataman en el Panathinaikos. En la que acaba de comenzar con el Valencia Basket ya ha demostrado que se ha liberado de los grilletes y volverá a ser una estrella de la Euroliga. En el estreno de la competición, el pequeño base hizo 26 puntos para liderar el triunfo taronja en la visita al Besiktas (94-96). Suya fue la canasta de la victoria, aunque aún restaba más de un minuto en el que se vieron errores por cada bando, incluidos dos tiros libres fallados por Omoruyi para empatar y otros dos por Taylor para sentenciar. Los turcos se encontraron 15 segundos para un último ataque. Nowell tuvo un triple para ganar sobre la bocina. Falló. Triunfo del Valencia Basket. Buen estreno de Xavi Albert como primer entrenador taronja. Shorts destacó sobre todos en un Valencia con las mismas señas de identidad que en la etapa de Pedro Martínez, incluido el trabajo coral. El base y otros cinco jugadores alcanzaron la decena de puntos. Entre ellos, Nikola Mirotic, que debutó de naranja metiendo 13 y siendo importante mediado el último cuarto, cuando el Besiktas ya había remontado y amenazaba con despegarse. Seis puntos seguidos del ala-pívot y una falta forzada en ataque fueron determinantes. Este Valencia que alineó a seis de sus nuevas caras, superó con madurez dos momentos críticos, uno en el primer cuarto y otro en el último. En el periodo inicial se vio ocho abajo (27-19) después de recibir un 12-3. Tras un tiempo muerto y con la pausa entre cuartos de por medio, respondió con parcial de 0-11. Shorts ya había hecho de las suyas y Brooks (10) era su cómplice. Después tomaron el testigo Taylor (12) y Rivero (10). Todos ellos llegaron con 10 puntos al intermedio. Y el Valencia, tres arriba (51-54). El tercer acto le perteneció casi por completo a Shorts, que amenazó ya con dos triples seguidos. Hizo 14 de los 27 puntos de su equipo, que firmó un sensacional 5/8 desde el arco. Uno de esos aciertos fue de un Mirotic que se desperezaba. Tanta puntería le dio al Valencia hasta 12 de ventaja (69-81). Al Besiktas le salvó la bocina y tras la pausa clavó cinco triples seguidos con un Morgan entonadísimo (15 puntos con 5/6). La diferencia, pese a los esfuerzos de Sako bajo el aro, se enjugó en un santiamén. Omoruyi adelantó a los locales (88-86) mientras la defensa cara a cara de Ugurlu neutralizaba a Shorts. El Besiktas se fue 91-86 tras otro triple, ahora de Wilbekin. El otro momento crítico. Y ahí apareció Mirotic. Taylor empató a 94 a falta de 2:03 y Shorts, en sus únicos puntos en el último cuarto, anotó en una entrada culminada en un escorzo imposible. Canastón. El de la victoria. El base encaja a la perfección en este Valencia. Ya es el líder. 94.- Besiktas (27+24+20+23): DeJulius (4), Nowell (17), Jeffries (-) Omoruyi (17), Zizic (4) -cinco inicial- Dotson (9), Morgan (15), Ugurlu (3), Birsen (-), Wilbekin (12), Brown (7), Gabriel (6). 96.- Valencia Basket (28+26+27+15): Shorts (26), Saint-Supèry (7), Taylor (12), Osetkowski (1), Reuvers (5) -cinco inicial- Rivero (10), Sako (10), Brooks (10), Moore (2), Puerto (-), Cárdenas (-), Mirotic (13). Árbitros: Mehdi Difallah, Ioannis Foufis y Luka Kardum. Sin eliminados. Incidencias: partido correspondiente a la primera jornada de la fase regular de la Euroliga disputado en el pabellón Turkcell Basketball Development Center de Estambul.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Hyped by Blazers in Return from Achilles Injury, 'He Looks Phenomenal'
articles.summary: Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard is heading back to the court soon enough after missing all of last season with a torn left Achilles tendon suffered during the 2025 playoffs.
articles.body:
Portland Trail Blazers guard Damian Lillard is heading back to the court soon enough after missing all of last season with a torn left Achilles tendon suffered during the 2025 playoffs.

He's already gotten some work in this summer with NBA players in advance of his long-awaited return.

Needless to say, folks are in awe of his efforts, per remarks relayed by Jason Quick of The Athletic.

"He looks phenomenal," Blazers head coach Micah Nori told Quick. "Every time I see him shoot the ball, I think it's going in."

Nori added: "If I never knew Dame Lillard, and I came into the building and just started watching them play basketball, I would not be able to tell he had any type of surgery.

Blazers forward Toumani Camara also had this to say.

"Impressive. Very, very impressive." He also remarked: "I think the most impressive thing for me was his first step, his speed, especially coming back from that injury. He was just very hard to guard all around."

Quick reported that Lillard has been taking part in daily runs at the Blazers' facility. In addition, Nori told Quick that he believes Lillard will fully participate (i.e. no limitations or restrictions) when training camp starts Tuesday, Sept. 29. That remark occurred after Lillard (and the rest of the team) underwent physicals last Wednesday.

The 36-year-old Lillard is a nine-time All-Star and seven-time All-NBA player who has averaged 25.1 points and 6.7 assists over his 13 NBA seasons. The 75th Anniversary Team member played in Portland for 11 campaigns before a trade request sent him to the Milwaukee Bucks for two years.

Now Lillard is back with Portland on a three-year deal as he hopes to lead the Blazers to greater heights. Portland bottomed out at 21-61 in 2023-24 but rose to 36-46 in 2024-25 before making the playoffs as a 42-win No. 7 seed last year.

The arrow continues to point up with Lillard in the mix and the addition of Nori, a well-respected and long-time assistant coach finally getting his chance as a head coach. If Lillard returns anywhere close to (or at) his old form, then that's a massive win for a Portland team that brings back a young core which got this team to the playoffs last year. The addition of Ja Morant via trade should also help matters.

Portland begins the season on Wed., Oct. 21 vs. the Phoenix Suns. By all accounts, Lillard should be starting and welcomed back with open arms by the home crowd.

articles.title: La Supercopa femenina alza el telón con el nuevo clásico: Valencia-Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: Helena Pueyo, exjugadora del equipo maño, pone el morbo en la primera semifinal (17.15 horas) e Innova-tsn Leganés y Hozono Global Jairis se miden en la segunda (20.00 h.)
articles.summary: Helena Pueyo, exjugadora del equipo maño, pone el morbo en la primera semifinal (17.15 horas) e Innova-tsn Leganés y Hozono Global Jairis se miden en la segunda (20.00 h.)
articles.body: La temporada nacional en el baloncesto femenino echa a andar este sábado con las semifinales de la Supercopa, que se disputará en el pabellón Jorge Garbajosa de Torrejón de Ardoz. Valencia Basket, Casademont Zaragoza, Hozono Global Jairis e Innova.tsn Leganés, que ejercerá de anfitrión, lucharán por el primer título del curso. En semifinales, duelo estelar entre dos de las grandes potencias del baloncesto femenino español en las últimas temporadas: Valencia Basket vs Casademont Zaragoza (17.15 horas). Ambos se han visto las caras recientemente luchando por títulos. De hecho, se midieron en las dos últimas finales de la Supercopa. Las taronjas ganaron en 2024 y las mañas, el año pasado. También será la reedición de las dos últimas finales de la Liga Femenina Endesa. Ahí vencieron las valencianas, que suman cuatro entorchados consecutivos. Con Javier Torralba iniciando nueva era en el banquillo esperan mantener ese dominio. En el epicentro del duelo estará la internacional Helena Pueyo, MVP de la última Supercopa, que este verano cambió Zaragoza por Valencia. El destino ha querido que su debut oficial como jugadora taronja sea contra sus ex. "Es algo emotivo por mis dos últimas temporadas", admitió la jugadora mallorquina en su presentación con su nuevo equipo. Enfrente, entre otras rivales, estará Mariona Ortiz, con la que ha compartido vestuario en la selección durante el Mundial de Berlín, cerrado con un bronce. Aprovechar el tirón de ese éxito es otro de los objetivos de la temporada. La segunda semifinal medirá a las anfitrionas del Innova.tsn Leganés y al Hozono Global Jairis (20.00 horas). Dos equipos buscarán dar la campanada en un torneo abierto y en el que los grandes no han alcanzado aún todo su potencial. La gran final, este domingo a las 17.00 horas. Todos los partidos se podrán ver por Teledeporte.

articles.title: Damian Lillard Drops New Song 'Nothing Without You' With Souls of Mischief, More
articles.summary: Damian Lillard is dropping more music ahead of his return to the Portland Trail Blazers.
articles.body:
Damian Lillard is dropping more music ahead of his return to the Portland Trail Blazers.

Lillard, under his stage name Dame D.O.L.L.A., collaborated with 1999 WRITE THE FUTURE and Souls of Mischief on a new song titled "Nothing Without You."

The latest single comes about five weeks after Lillard released a five-song collection titled Houston, We Have A Problem .

These latest projects come almost a decade after Lillard dropped his first full-length album, The Letter O, in 2016.

Lillard sat out the entirety of the 2025-26 season after suffering a torn left Achilles tendon in his final game with the Milwaukee Bucks.

He is preparing to open training camp next week before potentially seeing his first NBA action in over a year Oct. 21 during the Blazers' home opener against the Phoenix Suns.

articles.title: A’ja Wilson ‘flattens’ arena staffer before Aces game, shocking collision sparks stunned reactions from teammates and fans
articles.summary: WNBA star A’ja Wilson was involved in an awkward accident before the Las Vegas Aces faced the Phoenix Mercury on Thursday night, when she collided with an
articles.body: WNBA star A’ja Wilson was involved in an awkward accident before the Las Vegas Aces faced the Phoenix Mercury on Thursday night, when she collided with an arena staff member in the tunnel. Video from the scene showed the woman walking near a curtain as the Aces came out toward the court. Wilson ran into her, sending the staffer to the floor, while teammates reacted to the sudden collision. The woman quickly got back up, and the Aces continued to the court. Wilson then scored 34 points as Las Vegas completed a 100-82 regular-season win.A’ja Wilson collides with arena staffer as Las Vegas Aces enter courtThe incident happened before tipoff at the Mortgage Matchup Center in Phoenix. The video showed an arena staffer walking in front of a large curtain just as the Las Vegas players were preparing to run onto the court.Wilson was at the front of the group when she came through the curtain and collided with the woman. The impact sent the staffer to the floor. Chelsea Gray was visible behind Wilson and appeared to react to what had happened.According to the Daily Mail, the woman was able to stand up almost immediately. There was no report in the material reviewed of a serious injury to the staff member.The short clip then spread across X, where viewers focused on how the collision happened. One user wrote: ‘No, why is that lady there?! No one warned her the team are running out.’Another fan asked: ‘Why was she walking past in that moment anyways???’A third wrote: ‘Bruh… why was she just casually walking in front of it.’One viewer took the concern in another direction, writing: ‘Imagine injuring the greatest player of all time just before the playoffs sheesh.’A’ja Wilson scores 34 as Las Vegas Aces beat Phoenix MercuryWilson did not appear affected by the incident once the game began. She scored 17 points in the first quarter and had 21 by halftime as Las Vegas built a 65-36 lead.She made 16 of 28 shots, and her scoring helped Las Vegas build an early cushion.The Aces went on to beat the Phoenix Mercury 100-82 and finished the regular season with a 31-13 record. Wilson led the way with 34 points, while Jewell Loyd added 25 points off the bench. Stephanie Talbot scored 14 and Chelsea Gray had 12 points.The Associated Press reported that Las Vegas shot 56 per cent from the field and had 28 assists. The result left the Aces as the No. 3 seed for the WNBA playoffs, with Indiana Fever waiting in the first round.Phoenix ended its season at 16-28 after the loss. The Mercury had won the opening meeting between the teams 99-66, but Las Vegas won the final three games between them.Wilson’s 34-point night came after the unusual tunnel collision, making the pre-game moment only a small part of an otherwise strong finish to the Aces’ regular season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Warriors' Podziemski Could Crack ESPN's NBA Top 100 Next Season
articles.summary: According to ESPN's Zach Kram, Brandin Podziemski could crack ESPN's top-100 players next season, if he can make some improvements to his game.
articles.body:
Since entering the NBA as the 19th pick in the 2023 NBA Draft, Brandin Podziemski has carved out a solid role for himself within the Golden State Warriors rotation. He's proven himself to be a versatile talent capable of playing multiple positions and a range of roles. Yet, despite his versatility, Podziemski is often underrated by fans and the media alike.

Despite being overlooked for his contributions, ESPN's Zach Kram believes that if Podziemski can continue improving his game, he could break into ESPN's top-100 players by next summer.

"Even if Podziemski is unlikely ever to develop into a star, his all-around solid play makes him a valuable contributor," Kram wrote. "He can make open 3s, support Stephen Curry with secondary playmaking and hold his own on the defensive end. Even a moderate improvement in his age-23 season should place him firmly in Top 100 consideration next year."

Last season, Podziemski averaged 13.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 3.7 assists, shooting 53.1 percent from 2-point range and 37.1 percent from deep. Impressively, he played in all 82 regular-season games for Golden State, while posting a career-high 28.5 minutes per night.

Podziemski has become a key contributor for Kerr, emerging as a connector and high-level role player. It shouldn't take too much of a developmental leap for him to crack the NBA . Whether that changes how Podziemski is viewed by fans outside of the Warriors bubble is another question entirely, and in truth, shouldn't matter too much, especially if he helps Golden State make some noise in the postseason.
